# RdistNN

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/JakobJuergens/RdistNN/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/JakobJuergens/RdistNN/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![test-coverage](https://github.com/JakobJuergens/RdistNN/actions/workflows/test-coverage.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/JakobJuergens/RdistNN/actions/workflows/test-coverage.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

**RdistNN** estimates conditional treatment effects and regression functions
using distributional nearest-neighbor (DNN) weights. Choose covariate profiles,
fit local estimates, and inspect jackknife standard errors, local support and
tuning sensitivity. For causal estimation, you supply nuisance predictions;
the package constructs the adjusted signals and performs local estimation.

[Get started](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/articles/getting-started.html)
· [Function reference](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/reference/index.html)
· [Stata companion](https://github.com/JakobJuergens/RdistNN_stata)

## Installation

```r
install.packages("pak")  # once
pak::pak("JakobJuergens/RdistNN")
```

This installs production `master`, currently **0.1.0.9005**. R 4.1.0 or newer,
Rcpp and a C++17 compiler are required: Rtools on Windows, Xcode command line
tools on macOS, or an R-compatible compiler on Linux. For plots, also install
`ggplot2`; dashboards can use `patchwork`.

For reproducible installation, retain the full source commit or checked archive
identity; [RELEASING.md](https://github.com/JakobJuergens/RdistNN/blob/master/RELEASING.md)
explains candidate installation and historical pins.
The historical `v0.1.0` tag predates CLATE and the current shared reporting
interface. Retain the source commit or archive identity alongside your results.

## Choose a workflow

| Goal | Function | Main inputs |
|---|---|---|
| Conditional average treatment effects | `cate_dnn()` | Outcome, treatment and supplied outcome/propensity predictions, or a supplied pseudo-outcome |
| Conditional mean regression | `np_dnn()` | Outcome and covariates |
| Conditional effects among compliers | `clate_dnn()` | Outcome, binary treatment/instrument and instrument-arm nuisance predictions |
| Ratio of two local means | `affine_ratio_dnn()` | Two aligned signals |
| Two-scale regression | `np_tdnn()` | Outcome and two localization orders |
| Reusable DNN weights | `weights_matrix()` | Covariates and target profiles |

The estimators accept numeric matrices/vectors or data frames, including
tibbles. Select localization columns with `x_cols`; use `x0` for one profile
or `X0` for a matrix with one profile per row.

## A first CATE fit

This simulated example uses **oracle nuisance values**. In an application,
replace them with aligned predictions of the control outcome mean, treated
outcome mean and treatment propensity. RdistNN does not fit those models.

```{r cate}
library(RdistNN)

demo <- cate_demo_data(n = 180, p = 2, design = "hetero", seed = 1)
d <- demo$data
profiles <- cbind(X1 = seq(-0.5, 0.5, length.out = 5), X2 = 0)

fit_cate <- cate_dnn(
  data = d, x_cols = c("X1", "X2"),
  y_col = "Y", t_col = "D",
  m0_col = "m0_oracle", m1_col = "m1_oracle", e_col = "e_oracle",
  X0 = profiles, k = 1L, return = c("W", "dx", "nuisance")
)
summary(fit_cate)$coefficients
```

Each row reports the effect at one profile, its standard error and pointwise
confidence bounds. Inspect local support before interpreting a profile:

```{r cate-diagnostics}
as.data.frame(diagnostics(fit_cate))[, c("target_id", "n_eff", "treated_mass", "control_mass")]
```

With ggplot2 installed, the same fit gives a profile plot:

```{r cate-profile, eval = requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE), message = FALSE, dpi = 150, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.2, fig.alt = "CATE estimates at five X1 profiles with X2 fixed at zero, with pointwise confidence intervals."}
plot(fit_cate)
```

The [getting-started guide](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/articles/getting-started.html)
shows matrix inputs, supplied signals and covariance between prespecified
profiles. Earlier `m_col` calls should use both arm means for AIPW or a supplied
`pseudo_outcome`; a pooled outcome mean is not a substitute.

## Regression and conditional LATE

For a conditional mean, reuse the same covariates and targets without nuisance
inputs:

```{r regression}
fit_np <- np_dnn(data = d, x_cols = c("X1", "X2"), y_col = "Y", X0 = profiles)
data.frame(estimate = coef(fit_np))
```

Use `clate_dnn()` for conditional LATE with a binary instrument and treatment.
Supply the instrument propensity and the outcome/treatment means in each
instrument arm. The [CLATE guide](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/articles/conditional-late.html)
provides a complete example and explains the first-stage and status outputs.
Inspect the first stage alongside the ratio; weak local first stages can make
Wald intervals unreliable.

## Reporting, plots and tuning

CATE, regression and CLATE share `summary()`, `coef()`, `confint()`,
`predict()` and `diagnostics()`. Saved-fit prediction evaluates new profiles
using retained observations and signals. CATE and NP/TDNN expose joint target
covariance through `vcov()`; CLATE reports paired covariance for each target.

Use `plot_weights()` for localization, `plot_overlap()` for treatment or
instrument support, and `plot_tuning()` after a grid fit. See the
[plotting guide](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/articles/visualising-fits.html)
for retained-data requirements and dashboards. Saved objects retain
observation-level numeric data and inherit the data's sharing restrictions.

The default is exact DNN with `k = 1`. The order `s` controls localization:
larger `s` concentrates weight closer to the target. Set `s` explicitly or use
`tuning_mode = "grid"` for sensitivity comparisons; grids do not select a
preferred fit. Jackknife uncertainty requires `s < n`. The
[tuning guide](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/articles/kernel-order-tuning.html)
explains the default rule and candidate fits.

## Interpreting inference

Intervals are **pointwise**. The framework assumes independent observations;
cluster and survey-design inference are not supplied. Input row order breaks
equal-distance ties, so reordering tied observations can change a result.

Nuisance predictions must be aligned with the estimation observations.
Propensity clipping is numerical protection, not a remedy for poor overlap.
Diagnostics describe local support; they do not establish validity. For the
identification, nuisance-learning and localization conditions and theoretical
results, see the accompanying
[paper](https://jakobjuergens.com/research/#orthogonal-inference-conditional-z).
The package guides explain the corresponding inputs and outputs.

## Further reading and help

- [Notation and conventions](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/articles/notation-and-conventions.html): arguments, shapes and result fields.
- [Diagnostics and reporting](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/articles/diagnostics-reporting.html): support and uncertainty summaries.
- [Paper replication](https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/articles/paper-affine-replication.html): the study-specific bundle and saved evidence.
- PLQR, local IV-GMM and ratio confidence-set inversion remain **experimental**; use their dedicated reference pages.

Use `citation("RdistNN")` for references. Report problems through the
[issue tracker](https://github.com/JakobJuergens/RdistNN/issues) with a minimal
example and `sessionInfo()`. [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/JakobJuergens/RdistNN/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
covers development and numerical-engine contracts. RdistNN is licensed under
